newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares closed firmer on Monday, refusing to buckle following a profits warning from Philips, preferring instead to focus on a surge in Royal Dutch and a continuing winning streak on Wall Street.
"It wasn't a big surprise to hear Philips say things weren't going that well," said one dealer, adding the Royal Dutch rise more than outweighed the Philips fall.

Dealers said the 30-point gain on Wall Street by the Amsterdam close coupled with a steady dollar and bonds gave the market here a strong undertone. The AEX closed 1.71 points up at 588.91, well up from a session low of 584.98

Philips sent an early ripple of fear through the market, sparking a knee-jerk drop of 4.40 guilders to 60.40 during the morning with its announcement that second half operating profit was unlikely to improve as it had previously predicted.

Turnover in the stock bulged to 10.3 million shares, well above the more normal two to four million share daily volume. On the options market some 13,231 calls and 9,292 puts changed hands for 20.56 percent of the total turnover.
"The shares had been coming up a bit over the last two weeks after Cor Boonstra took over (as chairman on October 1), so we're back where we started with Philips," said a trader.

Analysts said the basic story behind Philips had changed little recently. "It's the old story -- price pressure and manufacturers fighting for market share, everything we've seen quite a few times before," said ING analyst Steven Vrolijk.

Philips shares had hauled themselves up from a year's low of 45.50, reached on July 25 -- the day it announced half year results and a restructuring involving the cutting of 6,000 jobs from its Sound & Vision unit over 18 months.
"I hope our clients were buying on 97 and 98 recovery prospects and not on Q3 and Q4 results. That's probably also why so far the Philips price is not that much down," he said.

Royal Dutch closed 4.50 guilders higher at 282.30, boosted by a rise in the oil price to its highest levels since January 1991, as renewed fighting broke out between rival factions in Iraqi Kurdistan.
"Royal Dutch has got a similar size weighting in the AEX as Philips and its gain was much bigger than the Philips loss so it's easy to see why the market didn't back off," a trader said.

Shipping group Smit Internationales closed 6.00 guilders higher at 99.00, boosted by news it agreed a $140 million-plus deal that involves selling its fleet of 49 off-shore supply ships to U.S. firm Seacor Holdings Inc.
Elsewhere financials were steady with Aegon up 90 cents to 88.50 guilders, ABN AMRO 20 cents higher at 96.80 guilders and ING 0.30 guilders stronger at 55.30.

Among the cyclicals Akzo was 2.40 guilders higher at 213.00 guilders and Hoogovens climbed 0.50 guilders to 65.20 while publisher Wolters Kluwer added 2.40 guilders to 215.80. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
